Raised when the content changes.
How long after a close a back request still counts as the second half of the same key press, in milliseconds.
The normal arrow, for the Select tool and tools that do not use the canvas yet.
A closed hand, while the view is being dragged.
A crosshair, for the shape tools that draw by dragging.
A pipette, while a color is picked from the canvas and for the Eyedropper tool. Its active point is the tip.
A magnifier, for the Zoom tool.
A magnifier with a minus, for the Zoom tool while Alt is held, because a click then zooms out.
An open hand, for the Hand tool.
A diagonal double arrow from top right to bottom left.
A double arrow pointing up and down, for the top and bottom handles.
A diagonal double arrow from top left to bottom right.
A double arrow pointing left and right, for the left and right handles.
A turning arrow, for the rotate handle.
A selection box smaller than this in both directions is a click on empty space.
A new shape needs at least this many screen pixels in x and in y.
The fill.
No pick is going on.
The stroke.
The most distance, in screen pixels, between two taps of a double-tap, and the most a finger may move during one tap.
The most time between two taps of a double-tap, in milliseconds.
How long the pointer must stay down, in milliseconds.
How far the pointer may move and still count as holding, in the units of the caller (dp).
Ends a closed outline.
A cubic bezier curve to a point, with two handle points.
A straight line to a point.
Starts the outline at a point.
A node was added. A drag that follows turns it into a smooth point.
The press hit the first node of a path with at least three nodes: the path is to be finished as closed.
The press landed on the last node (a double click or double tap): the path is to be finished as open.
The most colors the list keeps.
The most paths the list keeps.
Nothing is selected: the actions for the empty canvas.
Something is selected: the actions for the selection.
Upper limit for the number of ticks returned, to protect against huge lengths.
Minimum distance between two major ticks on screen, in pixels.
A path of lines and curves. The shape's PressToShape.App.Workspace.ScreenShape.Path holds its outline.
The size of the area that grabs a handle with a mouse or a pen, in screen pixels.
How far the rotate handle is from the top edge, in screen pixels.
The size of the area that grabs a handle with a finger, in screen pixels. The tablet layout can set its own through the theme.
The side of a handle in screen pixels.
The step of snapped rotation, in degrees.
The distance in document units that each paste moves the shapes further.
The one-finger action that was running must be cancelled without a result, because a second finger arrived or the gesture was cancelled.
Two fingers moved: zoom to TargetZoom around the previous midpoint, then move the view by the midpoint's change.
Nothing. The finger is not used.
The first finger moved: like a mouse move at X, Y.
The event is not a finger (mouse or pen). The caller handles it as usual.
The first finger went down: the active tool acts, like a mouse press at X, Y.
The first finger went up: like a mouse release at X, Y.
The part of the artboard, in screen pixels, that must stay visible on each axis.
The distance the view moves for a wheel delta of 1, in screen pixels.
The zoom factor for a wheel delta of 1.
Preset zoom steps in percent, ascending. Used by zoom in, zoom out and the zoom drop-down.
Whether a back request now is the second half of a press that already closed something. Answers true once for each close.
A menu or flyout was closed now.

Doc.Summary: Builds the shapes in drawing order: layers bottom first, shapes bottom first, so later shapes cover earlier ones. Groups are flattened: only the shapes in them are drawn, in order. Params.originY: Screen position of the artboard's top edge.
Params.enteredGroupId: The group that was entered. Shapes that are not inside it are marked as dimmed. null dims nothing.
Params.hiddenShapeId: A shape that is left out because a draft takes its place, for example a path that is being continued. null leaves nothing out.

On Android one press of the Back key arrives twice: as the Escape key, which closes an open menu or flyout by itself, and as the back request. If the Escape half already closed something, the back request must not do more (it would go on to ask about unsaved changes). The layout tells this guard when a menu or flyout closed; a back request right after that (within PressToShape.App.Workspace.BackRequestGuard.WindowMs) is the second half of the same press. The caller passes the time, so tests need no real time.

It works through interfaces for files, dialogs and messages, so it is tested without a UI. Parsing and serializing run off the calling (UI) context, and the file store does its reading and writing without blocking it. State changes happen on the calling context.

Doc.Summary: What the canvas has to do after a touch event, as decided by PressToShape.App.Workspace.TouchGestureTracker.

Decides what the fingers on the canvas mean. One finger acts with the active tool, like the mouse. A second finger cancels that action (so nothing stray stays in the drawing) and the two fingers then move and zoom the view around their midpoint. When a finger of the two lifts, the rest is ignored until every finger is up, so a lifting hand does not draw. Mouse and pen are not tracked. The tracker works on plain numbers and holds no document or view state. A pointer id only has to be unique from a finger's press to its release.

The math of the view over the drawing, on plain numbers in screen pixels: where the artboard is, how far the view may be moved, and what a zoom around a point does. The view offset (pan) is the distance of the artboard from its centered position. Non-finite input (devices can send it) never produces NaN or infinity.
Zoom limits, preset steps and fit calculation. Pure logic, values are percent.
